natural_body: 40% SMB discount: +31% signups, +18% rev, -12% ret; judge at renewal

first.rationale: Given limited experiment capacity, I'm prioritizing the direction that directly addresses the two internally-caused metrics currently declining (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), rather than reacting to competitor pricing pressure with promotional_pricing, which memory_73 shows carries an explicit retention cost (-12%) still unresolved at renewal judgment. Chasing price-sensitive SMBs with discounts risks compounding the retention problem and undermines sustainable long-term qualified revenue, the stated objective. Memory_31 and memory_86 both point to onboarding/signup simplification improving activation and time-to-value, but they may be describing overlapping or even the same underlying experiment lineage (signup field reduction vs. onboarding shortening), so I want to verify their original records to confirm they're independent supporting evidence rather than duplicated consolidation, before committing scale. I'm treating this as a standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout since onboarding changes interact with activation metrics in ways that need fresh confirmation given current quarter's declines, not just historical lift. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a plausible alternative but overlaps in mechanism with onboarding changes and is lower verification priority right now. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive don't address the acute SMB/activation pressure this week.
